solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 26dn.
Rather like a shadow leader of cabinet squeezed by stupid prat, Les

indicators.note: the leader of a group is its front member, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
something stupid is muddled and senseless, so the letters that follow are jumbled
a thing squeezed by others is pressed in between them, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the first letter of cabinet
the fodder letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the shadow cabinet leader is hemmed in by an idiot called Les.
explanation.walkthrough: The shadow cabinet is the opposition's team of would-be ministers, which lends 'shadow' its political misdirection; here it simply means a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral describes something ghostly and insubstantial, the quality of a phantom or wraith.

clue.text: ... in men was the likes of Dodi – horror!

definitions.text: in men was the likes of Dodi

blocks.clueFragment: in men was the likes of Dodi
blocks.note: the leading dots ask the solver to read the answer as the start of the sentence: Princess Diana's preference in men was the likes of Dodi Fayed
second meaning: strong dislike or revulsion

explanation.surface: A gossip-column remark that Princess Diana's choice in men ran to Dodi Fayed, followed by a shudder.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as DI'S TASTE, Di being Princess Diana, so the clue completes a sentence that begins with the answer itself. Dodi Fayed was her last companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is aversion or revulsion, a milder cousin of horror at something unpleasant.

clue.text: Civilians taken out by US military? All clear to Rocky

definitions.text: Civilians taken out by US military?

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaky, so the preceding letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical note that American forces killing civilians is waved through as fine by someone called Rocky.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocky looks like a name or nickname but signals the rearrangement. The definition leans on the military euphemism 'collateral damage', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Civilian deaths in a strike are euphemistically termed collateral damage, so the victims are, by this jargon, collateral.

clue.text: It's purpose is to make clients come to LHR – be worried

definitions.text: It's purpose is to make clients come

indicators.note: worried means fretted at and pulled about, so the preceding letters are tugged into another order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It reads like a travel advert's mission to draw clients to Heathrow, with a nervous traveller warned to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: LHR is the code for London Heathrow airport; the letters are just fodder. The definition's 'come' carries a smutty second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a house of prostitution whose business is giving paying customers sexual satisfaction.

clue.text: British ones ill equipped to, being cut by Labour's last exercises?

indicators.note: a word cut by a letter is split open so that the letter sits inside it
the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter of Labour is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Labour
ops, short for operations, are military exercises

explanation.surface: A jab at Labour for sending under-equipped British soldiers out on manoeuvres while cutting budgets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reflects the complaint, current at the time, that British soldiers in Iraq and Afghanistan lacked proper kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are soldiers, and the clue names British soldiers sent out without adequate kit.

clue.text: Dick, etc. when attending wedding

blocks.note: surface reading: a man named Dick and his friends going along to a wedding
setter's reading: the answer placed after 'wedding' makes a slang phrase for a man's genitals, of which dick is one example

explanation.surface: Dick and others turning up to a wedding as guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wedding tackle' is British slang for the male genitals; Dick is not a guest's name but a crude word for one part.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is equipment or gear, and in slang the male genital kit, so it covers dick and the rest.

clue.text: Utterly lacking in scandalous info. and shit, right

blocks.note: dirt is scandalous information, as in digging up dirt
poo is a childish word for excrement
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tabloid with no scandal to print and only rubbish to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly lacking in' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'lacking' and 'in' merely links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt-poor means extremely poor, lacking money and possessions almost entirely.

clue.text: (& 9/22dn.) Figure linked with row, best way of dealing with e.g. rebel Lib Dem MP voters?

definitions.text: Figure linked with row, best way of dealing with e.g. rebel Lib Dem MP voters?

blocks.note: a number, here three
a row is a line

blocks.clueFragment: best way of dealing with e.g. rebel Lib Dem MP voters
blocks.note: a whip is used to beat the disobedient, and a whip is also a party officer enforcing votes

explanation.surface: A coalition-era quip that rebellious Liberal Democrat MPs need a good thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament a whip is an instruction to vote; a three-line one, underlined three times, is the strictest. The clue also reads as recommending a beating for rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line whip is the strongest order a party gives its MPs to vote with the leadership, used to quell rebellions.

clue.text: see 8dn.
Cameron & co's "burial place," said recruit

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase before it is to be judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: Cameron and colleagues are the Cons (Conservatives); a burial place is a crypt

explanation.surface: A sneer about the Tory party's grave, then mention of a new recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron led the Conservative Party, abbreviated Con.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscript is someone compulsorily enlisted into the armed forces, a recruit by draft.

clue.text: Roof worker's arse over tip – drunk again?

indicators.note: arse over tip is slang for falling head over heels, so the word tumbles and reads the other way

blocks.note: a tiler lays roof tiles; the apostrophe-s just joins to what follows

explanation.surface: A roofer tumbling off the roof, and the question of whether he has been drinking again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit' is slang for drunk, so the answer read as lit once more means drunk again; its usual sense is set alight again, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit is slang for intoxicated, so with re- for repetition the answer whimsically means intoxicated a second time.

clue.text: Brenda's supposed style: tipping back the drink

indicators.note: tipping something back tilts it the opposite way, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose style is supposedly royal

explanation.surface: The Queen's supposed elegance as she knocks back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, here simply called the drink being knocked back.

clue.text: "Cannabis radicals", local rank and file party supporters

definitions.text: local rank and file party supporters

blocks.note: grass is slang for cannabis
a radical is a root, in mathematics and in word-building

explanation.surface: A headline about pot-smoking extremists among a party's local activists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radicals' looks political but is used in its root sense, from Latin radix.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass roots are the ordinary members of a party at local level, as opposed to its leadership.

clue.text: Dotty seen pressing ex-PM to put on a condom, say

definitions.text: to put on a condom, say

indicators.note: dotty means slightly mad, so the following letters are scrambled
pressing something means clasping it close, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: the fodder letters, to be rearranged
Edward Heath, Conservative Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A mad sighting of a former Prime Minister being urged to use protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath, a lifelong bachelor, is the ex-PM; the definition's 'say' marks putting on a condom as one example of sheathing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensheathe is to enclose in a sheath, and a condom is commonly called a sheath.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Really imaginative pre-PR fiddling by which some members hope to dodge prosecution

definitions.text: by which some members hope to dodge prosecution

indicators.note: fiddling means tinkering with or falsifying, so the preceding letters are tampered into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dig at MPs' creative fiddling of expenses and their hope of escaping charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddling' nods to the 2009 expenses scandal, when several MPs claimed this protection to avoid trial for false claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary privilege is the legal immunity members enjoy for proceedings in Parliament, which accused MPs tried to invoke in court.

clue.text: Gaddafi lost control of his corrupt Paris holding account – end of regime?

indicators.note: corrupt means debased or spoilt, so the letters lose their proper order
holding something means having it within, so one piece is placed inside the city name
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
AC is the abbreviation for account
the final letter of regime

explanation.surface: Libya's dictator loses command of a corrupt Paris bank account as his regime ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in 2011, when a NATO no-fly zone stripped Colonel Gaddafi of control over Libya's skies.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the sky above a country's territory, which the 2011 no-fly zone took out of Libyan command.

clue.text: Hitler's matchless piece of tackle?

blocks.note: surface reading: Hitler's unrivalled bit of equipment
setter's reading: according to the wartime song, Hitler had only one ball, so his was without a pair, and tackle is slang for the genitals

explanation.surface: Praise of some superb gear belonging to Hitler.
explanation.walkthrough: The British wartime song 'Hitler has only got one ball' supplies the joke; 'matchless' means unpaired, not peerless. 'Tackle' echoes 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A testicle is one of the male gonads, a component of the slang 'tackle'; Hitler's supposedly lacked its twin.

clue.text: Getting on with Clegg? Arch traitor!

blocks.note: getting on means ageing
Nick Clegg, Lib Dem leader and Deputy PM in the coalition

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone gets along with Clegg, then brands him a supreme betrayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on with' suggests friendship, but splits into ageing and a link. The jibe reflects anger at Clegg's coalition with the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil, Satan, who rebelled against God and is the archetypal betrayer.

clue.text: Randy feature of Wilson, Heath

indicators.note: a feature of something is a part of it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two surnames

explanation.surface: Speculation about which randy trait belonged to Prime Ministers Harold Wilson and Ted Heath.
explanation.definitionFit: On heat describes a female animal ready to mate, and by extension anyone sexually aroused.

clue.text: To endure an ex-minister – that would be unbearable

blocks.note: to last is to endure
Jack Straw, former Labour Home and Foreign Secretary

explanation.surface: Having to put up with a former minister would be intolerable.
explanation.walkthrough: The ex-minister is Jack Straw, who served in Blair's and Brown's cabinets.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final burden that makes a situation intolerable, from the proverbial camel's broken back.

clue.text: Extra coy tosser

blocks.note: first meaning: more bashful
second meaning: one who shies, that is throws, things

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at an especially bashful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosser' is a British insult, but here it is literal: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of shy means more timid, while the agent noun names a person who throws.

clue.text: see 8dn
Large room also turned on Brown finally

indicators.note: turned means twisted out of place, so the preceding letters are rearranged
finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the surname is kept

blocks.note: the fodder letters, to be rearranged
the final letter of Brown

explanation.surface: A big room also rounding on Gordon Brown at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like part of 'turned on', meaning attacked, but it only places the last letter after the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a large reception room in a grand house, used for receiving guests.

clue.text: Maybe Yoko's after neutral sex

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters are only one possible version of the name, so they may be rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for neutral
the fodder letters, to be rearranged; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A suggestion that Yoko Ono is after gender-neutral sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the rearranged name behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooky is British slang for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: see 15ac.
(& 1dn.) Cyclops' organ's fluffy stuff, as the game caller says

blocks.note: the one-eyed Cyclops has a single eye
the apostrophe-s supplies its letter
down is soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: The setter describes his own organ as fluff, in the voice of a bingo caller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes down' is the call at the start of a game of bingo, telling players to watch their cards. Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes down is the bingo caller's traditional opening cry, signalling play is beginning.

clue.text: Rather cheap hack linked to Katie?

blocks.note: to hack is to cut
Katie Price, the glamour model also known as Jordan

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist tied to Katie Price, which looks rather tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist but is the verb for chopping. Katie Price is a British glamour model and reality TV personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut-price means sold at a reduced price, hence cheap.

clue.text: Prince no longer keen to grab Brenda's crown

indicators.note: grabbing something seizes and holds it, so one piece goes inside the other
a crown sits on top, so it is the head or opening letter of the name

blocks.note: keen means sharp, wide awake
the first letter of Brenda

explanation.surface: A prince who has lost his enthusiasm for snatching the Queen's crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen. 'No longer keen' looks like one phrase, but 'no longer' belongs with 'Prince'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, Victoria's consort, died in 1861, so he is a prince who is no more.
